patch_description: The current program recomputes all 286 triangle areas on every annealing step (wasting most of its 2500-iteration budget on redundant computation) and initializes from a single perturbed grid. The new version: (1) maintains a cache of all triangle areas and incrementally updates only the 66 triples containing the moved point (with a partial-min trick), making each step ~5x cheaper so we can afford ~30k iterations across 6 independent restarts; (2) uses boundary-heavy structured initializations (points on an ellipse plus interior center, and a 3-fold symmetric triangular layout) known to be favorable for Heilbronn-type problems, instead of only one grid seed; (3) uses an adaptive step/temperature schedule with greedy final polish; (4) keeps deterministic seeding (seed=42) and rescales the final configuration so the convex hull has unit area. More search, smarter starts, and incremental evaluation directly target the primary metric (min_area_normalized) while staying within time constraints.
